newsitem.title: USA: Teva says MS drug approved by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Teva says MS drug approved by FDA.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. of Israel said Monday it has won approval to sell Capoxone, used to treat a form of multiple sclerosis, in the United States from the federal Food and Drug Administration.
The drug, used to treat relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis, will be available in this country early next year, Teva said.
Capaxone was approved in Israel earlier this year and will become available by the end of 1996, said the company based in Petah-Tiqva, Israel.
It will be sold in the United States by Teva Marion Partners, a partnership between Teva and Hoechst Marion Roussel Inc., the company said.
Teva stock rose 93.75 cents to $45.375 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
